name: Wren Ximenez
summary: A 34-year-old former Army military police sergeant who runs Vira's day watch from the front gatehouse and supervises fifteen officers, most of them older than he is. He's careful, fair and very serious, lives alone on Desert Willow Way in Saltbrush, runs before dawn, and still says 'ma'am' more than he means to.

backstory.childhood: Born February 18, 1992, at the Army hospital at Fort Huachuca, Arizona, and raised between Sierra Vista and his grandmother's house in Tucson. His mother named him after the cactus wrens nesting in the saguaro outside the hospital window, and he took a lot of grief for it in middle school and learned early to end fights fast and without much fuss. He was the oldest of three and the one who made sure his younger sisters got on the bus while his father was deployed.
backstory.family_of_origin: His father, Hector Ximenez, is a retired Army first sergeant whose family came from Colon, Panama, a man of rules, early mornings and very few words, now 63 and fishing in Sierra Vista. His mother, Denise, 61, is a Black woman from Tucson who spent thirty years as a school nurse. She talks enough for both of them and calls Wren every Sunday after church to ask whether he's eaten a vegetable. His sister Simone is a pharmacist in Phoenix. His sister Kiara, the youngest, is 27 and the one everybody worries about. She's been sober two years, and Wren sends her money he tells nobody about.
backstory.education: Buena High School in Sierra Vista, class of 2010: varsity cross-country, Junior ROTC, and a 3.4 GPA that disappointed his mother. He enlisted at 18. He finished a bachelor's in criminal justice online through Arizona State in 2019, mostly at night in the guard shack of his last job, and he still has the coffee-ringed textbooks. Since then he's added an armed guard license, a defensive tactics instructor certificate and a supervisor course Vira paid for.
backstory.before_vira: Army military police from 2010 to 2016. He was stationed at Fort Hood, deployed to Afghanistan in 2012 to 2013 on base security and convoy escort, and finished at Fort Bliss as a sergeant running a patrol squad. He got out at 24 because he was engaged and his fiancee, Dana, wanted him home. They moved to Lancaster, California, and he worked contract security at a big solar plant in the Mojave for four years on the overnight post. Dana left in 2019. She said, kindly, that he'd come home from the Army and never really arrived, and he has never been able to decide whether she was right.
backstory.how_they_came_to_vira: In the spring of 2020, with the solar plant contract changing hands and his own life emptied out, he saw the Vira posting for day-watch security. It was a new hyperscale site, it paid better, and it was nowhere near anything that reminded him of Dana. He interviewed in a mask and started in June 2020. He rented a place in Saltbrush and bought the house on Desert Willow Way in 2022. He made sergeant of day watch in the summer of 2023, at 31, over three officers with more years than him, including Gus Weatherby.
turning_points: Afghanistan, 2012. He stopped a vehicle at a checkpoint that turned out to be nothing and has thought about how close he came to getting it wrong almost every week since. It made him slow and deliberate on purpose.
Dana leaving in 2019. He stopped drinking alone, started running every day, and started going back to church, all inside the same month.
Making sergeant in 2023 and realizing that the job was mostly people, and that people were harder than checkpoints.
Felix Haskie almost quitting in 2023. Wren sat in the gatehouse with him for an hour after shift and talked him out of it, and found out he was good at the part of the job he'd been dreading.

household_notes.note: 101 Desert Willow Way: a two-bedroom stucco house with a carport he swept himself and a kitchen he keeps cleaner than any barracks. The second bedroom is a library and a weight bench. Military history, mostly, alphabetized. He eats dinner at the counter standing up most nights, which his mother would hate. He's fostered cats for the animal rescue in Halcyon twice and given both back, because he decided he wasn't home enough. His friend Talia Quintero has a key and leaves him leftovers in the fridge in labeled containers.

traits: quietly funny once he trusts you
values: doing what you said you'd do
protecting his people, even from themselves
fears: Making the wrong call under pressure and someone getting hurt
Being exactly the kind of man Dana described
personality.humor: Deadpan and rare. He'll say something perfectly dry over the radio, like 'Gate copies the coyote, coyote is not on the access list,' and people will replay it for a week. With friends he's sillier than anyone expects and does an excellent impression of his father.
personality.temper: He almost never shows it. When he's angry he gets very formal, very slow and very specific, and that's worse. He writes everything down. He's raised his voice at work exactly once, at a contractor who drove through the lift arm in 2021.
quirks: Arrives at the gatehouse at 5:30 for a 6:00 shift, every day
Keeps the crew's birthdays and kids' names in a pocket notebook and reviews it before briefing
Can't stop saying 'ma'am' and 'sir' and apologizes for it
Irons his uniform shirt even though it's a polo
Runs exactly five miles every morning at 4:15, even in August, with a headlamp

voice.how_they_talk: Measured, low and clear. He pauses before answering, and the pause is real, because he's thinking. He speaks in complete sentences and gives the reason with the order: 'Hold the truck at the lane, because the badge didn't scan.' On the radio he's crisp and textbook. Off it he's softer and a little shy, and he'll ask you a question about yourself rather than talk about himself.
voice.vocabulary: Military and security plainness: 'understood,' 'affirmative' when he slips, 'post,' 'relief,' 'squared away.' He doesn't swear at work. He quotes his father ('Slow is smooth, smooth is fast') and occasionally scripture, quietly and without preaching. He reads, so bigger words show up when he's comfortable.
phrases: Let's slow down and walk it through.
Write it the way it happened, not the way you wish it happened.
Yes, ma'am. Sorry. Noor. Yes, Noor.
voice.with_strangers: Courteous, formal and impossible to rattle. Truck drivers who show up without paperwork find him polite and completely immovable. He smiles more than people expect, and it doesn't change the answer.
voice.with_friends: Looser, more curious and a good listener. He teases Talia mercilessly and lets Ray drag him to the saloon in Saltbrush once a month. He'll show up at 2 AM if you call, and he won't mention it afterward.

daily_life.workday: Alarm at 3:55, five miles on the highway shoulder and the streets of Saltbrush with a headlamp and a reflective vest, a shower, two eggs and black coffee. On the road by 4:50 and at the gatehouse by 5:30. He reads the night watch's log, checks the gate lane and lift arms himself, and holds the day-watch briefing at 5:55 with patrol assignments, deliveries expected, contractors on site and anything odd from the night. Then he runs the gatehouse: badge exceptions, visitor escorts, delivery trucks routed to receiving, radio traffic from the patrols and the camera wall, incident reports reviewed and signed. He eats lunch at his desk. He does at least one walking loop of the staff lot and the halls every shift so the crew sees him out there. At 2:00 he hands off to the swing sergeant and usually stays until 2:30 finishing paperwork.
daily_life.after_work: A nap, which he's ashamed of. Reading. Dinner, sometimes with Talia before her night shift, when they eat at the taco shop in Saltbrush at 4:30 like retirees. He's in bed by 8:30.
daily_life.days_off: His two days off rotate with the watch schedule. Long runs in the hills off the highway. Church on Sundays at the church in Saltbrush, back pew. Yard work and errands at the hardware store and the grocery. A Saturday a month driving to Halcyon for a used bookstore, a real gym and a movie by himself. He calls his mother, his sisters and his father, in that order, and the call with his father takes four minutes.
hobbies: Distance running, including a desert half-marathon every spring
Military and American West history, especially the Civil War and the Indian Wars
Birdwatching, privately, with his grandfather's binoculars, cactus wrens included. He hasn't told anyone at work.
daily_life.food: Eggs, rice, black beans and chicken, the same things most days. His mother's peach cobbler at Thanksgiving and nowhere else. The taco shop in Saltbrush with Talia. Whatever labeled leftovers she leaves in his fridge.
daily_life.music: Old gospel from his grandmother's house, Marvin Gaye and Al Green, and nineties hip-hop on long runs. He has a Panamanian salsa playlist his father made him that he plays when he cleans and denies owning.
hangouts: The highway shoulder north of Saltbrush at 4:15 AM
The back pew of the church in Saltbrush
The taco shop in Saltbrush, the corner table
The saloon in Saltbrush, once a month, with Ray

work.what_they_actually_do: Sergeant of day watch, 6 AM to 2 PM. He supervises fifteen officers across the gate lane, interior hall patrol, roving campus patrol, perimeter foot patrol and the camera wall in the security office. He builds the post assignments, runs briefings, handles badge and visitor exceptions at the front gatehouse, signs every incident report, trains new hires, writes evaluations, does discipline when it's needed, and coordinates with facilities and operations when something physical goes wrong, like a stuck lift arm, a dead camera or a door contact that won't clear.
work.how_good_they_are: Very good, and better every year. He's steady in an incident and consistent with discipline, which the crew respects even when they don't like it, and he's a natural teacher one on one. His weakness is that he holds too much himself, rarely delegates the paperwork, and gives the benefit of the doubt a little too long. Noor has told him so.
work.how_they_feel_about_the_job: Proud of it. It's the first job since the Army where he feels he's building something, a crew that works. Some days it's lonely being the boss of people old enough to be his parents, and he has nobody at his own level on site to talk to.
work.opinion_of_vira: Well funded, well built and run by serious people. He doesn't know what's in the halls and considers that above his post. He's proud that day watch has had no serious breach on his shift. He's mildly bothered by how much of the site runs itself, and by the handful of times it ran itself in ways nobody could explain to him.
work.ambition: Site security manager someday, at Vira or somewhere like it. He's thought about the state police academy and talked himself out of it twice. Privately he'd like to be married again by 40, and he doesn't know how to start.

relationships.name: Noor Rojas
relationships.history: Noor started on roving patrol in March 2023, a few months before he made sergeant. On her first day he called her 'ma'am' eleven times. She counted, and on the twelfth she told him to pick a different word, and Felix laughed so hard at the lift arm he had to turn around. She came from years of hospital security leadership and could have put in for sergeant herself. She didn't, and she backs him in front of the crew even when she'd do it differently. They disagreed in November 2025 when Pete Iniguez propped the Hall C2 loading door with a trash can: she wanted it written, and he gave Pete a verbal. He listened to her, kept his decision, and still uses her incident reports to train every new hire.
relationships.how_they_feel: He respects her more than anyone on the crew and is a little intimidated by her. She's the person he checks his judgment against. He suspects she's right about Pete and is waiting to be proven wrong.

relationships.name: Talia Quintero
relationships.history: They met in 2021 at the church in Saltbrush, where she was a Saltbrush girl working at the pharmacy and he was the new guy in the back pew who didn't sing. She ran the coffee table after the service and kept refilling his cup until he talked to her. He's the one who told her Vira was hiring technicians, and she started on Crew D nights in 2024. Everybody in Saltbrush assumes they're dating. They aren't, and they've never been, and they find it funny. She has a key to his house. He drives her to the doctor in Halcyon when she needs a ride.
relationships.how_they_feel: His best friend, the person he'd call first for anything. She's the only one who can tell him he's being an idiot and have him listen. He'd do anything for her, and he worries about her driving home at 6:15 AM after twelve hours of nights.

relationships.name: Felix Haskie
relationships.history: Felix joined day watch in 2022 at 24 on the gate lane, and Wren took him on from day one. In 2023, after Felix's daughter Lily was sick for months and he'd been late four times, he came in ready to quit. Wren sat in the gatehouse with him for an hour after shift, worked out a month of 7 AM starts for him with Kim Rasmussen watching the gate lane from the camera wall for the first hour, and told him he was the best badge-checker on the crew, which was true. Felix has run the gate lane ever since and has started training the new officers on it himself.
relationships.how_they_feel: Like a younger brother, and like proof that the job matters. Wren is quietly preparing him to be sergeant someday and hasn't told him.

relationships.name: Abe Sandoval
relationships.history: Abe came to Vira in 2025 at 47 after twenty years of other work, and he's on perimeter foot patrol. He was solid on the fence and terrible at incident reports, so Wren spent his first three months sitting with him after shift going line by line through Abe's writeups, until Abe could write one Wren didn't have to send back. It's an odd mentorship, the younger man teaching the older one, and Abe has been gracious about it.
relationships.how_they_feel: Respect, and some embarrassment at being his teacher. He admires Abe's patience on the long fence walks in the heat and is proud of how far his reports have come.

relationships.name: Ray Navarro
relationships.history: Ray is a Crew B technician in Hall A4. They met in late 2024 when Ray's dog got loose in the staff lot and Wren caught it at the lift arm. Ray runs too, and since then they've done a Sunday long run together when their days line up. Ray is the one who drags Wren to the saloon in Saltbrush once a month to watch a fight on the TV.
relationships.how_they_feel: Easy, fun and uncomplicated. Ray gets him out of the house. Wren thinks Ray takes nothing seriously and envies him for it.

relationships.name: Gus Weatherby
relationships.history: Gus has been on day watch since 2021, doing interior patrol through the halls, and he commutes an hour from Halcyon. In 2023 he and Wren both put in for sergeant. Wren got it. Gus shook his hand that afternoon and said, 'Better you than me, kid, I like sleeping,' and has backed him since. They talk football at briefing.
relationships.how_they_feel: Grateful and a little guilty. He knows Gus wanted it more than he admits. He trusts Gus with the halls completely.

relationships.name: Omar Bustamante
relationships.history: Omar walks the perimeter fence on foot and has done since 2024. He's a former Marine, 53, from Ironwood. He and Wren found each other early through the service and trade the old Army-versus-Marines insults at briefing. Omar's the one who taught him where the coyotes den along the south fence.
relationships.how_they_feel: Comfortable. Omar is the only one on the crew he can talk to about deployment, and they do, rarely, in the shade of the gatehouse after shift.

relationships.name: Kim Rasmussen
relationships.history: Kim has run the camera wall in the security office since 2021, one of the longest-serving officers on day watch and the oldest at 59. In 2023, when Wren asked, she watched the gate lane on camera for Felix's first hour for a month. She's raising a four-year-old, Aaliyah, and Wren has bought the child more birthday presents than is strictly professional.
relationships.how_they_feel: Respectful and fond. She's the eyes of his watch. He'll miss her terribly when she retires, and he knows Noor wants her seat.

relationships.name: Pete Iniguez
relationships.history: Pete joined day watch in fall 2025 on interior hall patrol. He's charming, a good talker and sloppy on doors. In November 2025 Noor found the Hall C2 loading door propped with a trash can while Pete was in the cafeteria. Wren gave him a verbal warning instead of a written one, partly because Pete's wife works the county road crew and money is tight. Pete has been on thin ice since.
relationships.how_they_feel: He wants Pete to work out and doubts it more every month. He knows the verbal cost him something with Noor.

relationships.name: Trent Rojas
relationships.history: Noor's husband, a Crew B facilities engineer who passes the gatehouse most mornings with a wave and a flash of his brights. On Trent's first day in December 2024 he kissed Noor through her SUV window right at the gatehouse, and Wren has brought it up at least once a season since.
relationships.how_they_feel: Likes him. Trent is friendly with everyone, and Wren finds it a little exhausting and a little enviable.

relationships.name: Wes Underhill
relationships.history: Wes lives next door with two small kids and a roommate who's a part-time pastor at the church. He works Crew C nights, so he pulls in as Wren is leaving for his run, and they nod across the carports at 4:15 AM.
relationships.how_they_feel: He worries about Wes, a young father on nights, and has quietly mowed his strip of lawn more than once.

wants: To be site security manager by 40
To be married by 40, and to be someone a person would want to come home to
His sister Kiara to stay sober
To run a full marathon, finally
worries: That he's too young for this job and everyone knows it
That being the boss has made him lonelier than the Army did
That he'll make the wrong call on a real incident
That the lift arms opening by themselves means something he's not seeing
secrets: He sends Kiara three hundred dollars a month and none of his family knows
He still has Dana's ring in a drawer in the library bedroom
Some mornings on the 4:15 run he stops on the highway shoulder and cries for a minute, and he doesn't know why, and then he finishes the five miles
He applied to the state police academy in 2022, was accepted, and never went
inner_life.regrets: Dana, and the version of himself who came home from Afghanistan and wouldn't talk. He also regrets that Gus didn't get the sergeant job, because he thinks Gus would have been happier.

health_and_money.health: Very fit: resting heart rate in the fifties, a left knee that complains after long runs, and an ankle he broke at Fort Hood. He sleeps six hours and calls it eight. He's had a VA disability rating for tinnitus since he got out and still hears a hum when the gatehouse is quiet. Through the VA in Halcyon he saw a counselor for a year after Dana left, and he doesn't talk about that.
health_and_money.money: Solid. A sergeant's pay, the VA disability check, a mortgage on Desert Willow Way at a rate he locked in during 2022, an SUV with a year left on it, and no other debt. He maxes his 401k. The three hundred a month to Kiara is the only unplanned line in his budget.

beliefs.faith: Raised AME by his grandmother in Tucson and lapsed through the Army. He came back after Dana left. He attends the church in Saltbrush most Sundays from the back pew, reads a psalm most mornings after his run, and has been asked twice to usher and said no both times. His faith is quiet and practical, and he doesn't bring it up at work.
beliefs.politics: Registered Republican out of a family habit, more of a moderate in practice: pro-veteran, pro-police with a lot of opinions about training, and uneasy with the shouting on both sides. He keeps politics out of the gatehouse entirely and asks his crew to do the same.

knowledge.about_vira: He knows the security side completely: every access point, every lift arm and gate lane, the badge system's quirks, the camera coverage, the perimeter fence and its weak spots, the delivery routes to receiving, and which contractors are on site this week. He knows the place came online in 2019, a year before he arrived, and that day watch was barely organized when he started. He doesn't know what the halls do and doesn't ask.
knowledge.about_lyra: He has never heard the name Lyra. He believes Vira runs on ordinary automation and the badge system. Over six years he's logged a handful of lift-arm openings at the front gatehouse with no badge scan and no vehicle in the lane. Most were mid-afternoon, and one was at 5:40 AM while he stood next to it. Facilities called them sensor faults and replaced a loop detector in 2024. He accepted that on paper and still glances at the arm when it's quiet.
knowledge.about_marcus: He knows Marcus by sight and by badge as one of the staff who rides a motorcycle in from Saltbrush. Wren checks him through the lane like anyone else, and they've never spoken beyond 'morning.'
rumors_they_believe: That the south fence was cut in 2021 before he had the authority to see the report
That operations is going to install license-plate readers and replace half the gate lane staff
That a new block of halls is coming south of the solar field

memories.what: His first day at Vira, in a mask, at a gatehouse with half the cameras not yet online. He spent the shift drawing his own map of the campus on the back of a visitor log.
A Sunday at the church in Saltbrush when Talia Quintero refilled his coffee four times after the service until he finally asked her name. She said, 'Took you long enough.'
The afternoon he was named sergeant. Gus Weatherby shook his hand in the security office and said 'Better you than me, kid,' and Kim Rasmussen cut him a slice of the cake she'd somehow already baked.
An hour in the gatehouse after shift with Felix Haskie, who'd come in with a resignation letter in his pocket. They walked out together at 3:30 and the letter went into the trash can by the lift arm.
Noor Rojas's first day. He called her 'ma'am' eleven times, she counted, and she told him on the twelfth to pick a different word. Felix had to turn around at the lift arm because he was laughing.
Trent Rojas kissing Noor through her SUV window at the gatehouse on his first day. Wren stood at the arm and looked carefully at the sky.
Catching Ray Navarro's loose dog at the lift arm with a granola bar. Ray came jogging up the lane in sandals, and they agreed to go running together the next Sunday.

Standing next to the front lift arm doing his preshift check when it rose all the way up with no badge and no car in the lane, held, and came back down. He logged it, sent a ticket to facilities, and stood there for a while after.

Hearing Noor's voice through the security office door, raised for the first time, at Pete Iniguez over the propped Hall C2 door. He decided on a verbal warning that afternoon and has second-guessed it ever since.
Sitting with Abe Sandoval after shift going through Abe's ninth draft of a fence report, until Abe wrote one Wren signed without a single change. Abe framed it as a joke and hung it in his locker.

conversation_starters: Ask him why he gets to the gatehouse at 5:30
Mention birds and watch him decide whether to admit it
Ask what the Army taught him that's actually useful here
Ask about the lift arm that opens by itself, and he'll say 'sensor fault' slowly
Ask him about Talia and he'll say 'we're not dating' before you finish
